notes: Intro: Evaluating Redwood for migration from current LLM provider (OpenAI) — started as Hosted API evaluation, strong interest in eventual Dedicated/reserved capacity
Motivation: cost predictability + lower per-token unit economics at scale; need better routing/quiet-degradation during bursts; want unified path from hosted -> dedicated
Workloads: primary is conversational support assistant (latency-sensitive), secondary is doc search + summarization for internal knowledge base

Targets: P95 latency <= 400ms on short chat turns (<=256 tokens), throughput ~ 50 concurrent chat sessions per region, cost-sensitivity moderate (aim to reduce per-token cost by 30% vs current), steady-state ARR drive
Model preference: currently using GPT-4-style family on provider; evaluating equivalent open models via Redwood catalog; need ability to pin model versions and fallback to smaller/quantized variant

POC summary (Hosted): completed lightweight POC 2025-11-05 — integrated via Redwood OpenAI-compat endpoints, ran 2k chat sessions + 10k embeddings. Observations: fast onboarding, streaming OK, prefix caching gave 15% token savings

Prompt parity/Regression work: ran test suite of 120 seed prompts (support templates/finance templates). 8 prompts showed deviation (tone/length/hallucination) vs baseline. SEs recommended model tuning + prompt rework. Action: run parallel evaluation on Dedicated quantized variants

Compatibility notes: Redwood's compatibility layer mapped headers + system messages; had to adjust role handling for certain function-calling flows; some API surface differences documented in drive deck
Security & Compliance: procurement needs SOC2 doc + KMS integration plan; Legal asked for data residency details for EU customers (they have EU customers), plan to use VPC/Dedicated for residency

Pricing conversations: Redwood provided both Hosted usage quote and Dedicated reserved tier model. Hosted cost acceptable for trial; Dedicated needs committed spend (~$120k/yr) to hit target economics. Negotiating ramp credits and trial reserved window

Timeline/engagements: AE demos (2025-10-15), Hosted POC kickoff (2025-11-01), POC results & technical deep dive with SE (2025-11-05), Security scoping call with Redwood security (2025-11-20), Pricing review w/ finance (2025-12-02), Legal redlines started (2025-12-08)
Quotes from calls: 'We need parity on tone and hallucination rates before we flip production traffic' — Head of ML; 'Budget needs sign-off by finance for dedicated commit' — CTO
Open items: final regression checklist (subset of 8 failing prompts) + acceptance thresholds, Dedicated SLA for 99th pct latency, contractual data residency clause, KMS/HSM key rotation plan
Canary plan: 2-week Dedicated canary with 10% production traffic -> monitor latency/cost/quality, rollback policy to Hosted compatibility endpoints if regressions exceed thresholds
Internal stakeholders: Product (Eva - PM), Head of ML (Jamal), CTO (R. Patel), SRE (Yvonne) — heavy technical involvement required for migration
Competitive risk: if Redwood parity issues persist, team may extend contract with current provider and adopt hybrid approach (OpenAI for chat, Redwood for embeddings)
